login.title: Sign in to bosun
login.subtitle: Node panel
login.hint: The initial password is in bosun's first-start log; run bosun admin reset-password if it is lost.

mode.title: Mode
mode.fixedHint: panel.driver in config.yaml is fixed to {{driver}}; this panel is read-only. Set it to local to switch modes here.
mode.managedHint: Captain manages this node. Inbounds, users and forwards are edited in the panel; this UI is read-only.
mode.adoptHint: Get a pair code from “Add node” in Captain. The current inbounds, users and forwards are snapshotted first; the panel pushes its own state afterwards.
mode.adoptConfirm: Local config is disabled and saved as a snapshot; cores restart on the panel's state. Continue?
mode.detachConfirm: The panel loses control of this node; pairing again is needed to re-adopt. Continue?
mode.keepHint: The last state the panel pushed becomes the local config; otherwise the pre-takeover snapshot is restored.
mode.restoreHint: The snapshot taken before takeover will be restored.
mode.emptyHint: No snapshot: the node comes back empty.

inbounds.title: Inbounds
inbounds.subtitle: Protocol servers this machine offers. Saving applies immediately, no restart.
inbounds.emptyHint: No inbounds yet. Click “Add inbound” and pick a recipe.
inbounds.serverNameTls: Needs a certificate for this name: upload one on the Certificates page or configure certs in config.yaml
inbounds.trafficPatternHint: mita's trafficPattern, passed through as is. Fields: seed, unlockAll, tcpFragment{enable, maxSleepMs 0-100}, nonce{type RANDOM|PRINTABLE|PRINTABLE_SUBSET|FIXED, applyToAllUDPPacket, minLen/maxLen 0-12, customHexStrings}, padding{maxMiddlePaddingLen, maxEndPaddingLen 0-255}, lowEntropy{mode OFF|32|40|48|56, maskRotation}. Unset fields are generated by mieru from the seed.
inbounds.displayHint: When the entrance is elsewhere (an IPLC front door forwarding here), share links use this address and port.
inbounds.ingressDirectHint: Clients dial this node's public address.
inbounds.ingressNewHint: The line ingress is created first, then the inbound.
inbounds.ingressNewFields: Copy these from the provider's network information page:
inbounds.recipeHint: Pick a recipe to fill the fields and generate keys; edit anything afterwards.

recipes.vlessRealityDesc: Best TCP stealth; no certificate needed.
recipes.hysteria2Desc: QUIC, best throughput on lossy lines; needs a certificate.
recipes.mieruDesc: Low-signature TCP for IPLC and carrier QoS.
recipes.ss2022Desc: Lightweight; server key generated for you.
recipes.anytlsDesc: New protocol resisting traffic analysis; needs a certificate.
recipes.snell5Desc: Surge's official snell-server, one shared PSK generated for you.

inbounds.serverNameAuto: Domain of the certificate; its DNS must point at this machine
inbounds.autoCertHint: Obtained and renewed from Let's Encrypt; no certificate files to manage
inbounds.acmeHttp: HTTP (port 80 here must be reachable from the internet)
inbounds.lineOnlyHint: This node has no public address and is reached only through a line ingress: pick one, or share links have no usable address.
inbounds.mieruStrategyHint: The three nobrand-oneclick presets: dedicated line = no obfuscation, public = conservative, stealth adds fragmentation and padding; custom edits traffic_pattern directly.
inbounds.mieruBothHint: TCP on this port, UDP on {{port}} (port + 1); open both
inbounds.mieruMtuHint: Blank = 1400; only matters for the UDP transport, 1280–1500
inbounds.mieruMuxHint: Client parameter written into share links; blank leaves it to the client (usually LOW)
inbounds.mieruHandshakeHint: no-wait is 0-RTT (lower latency); standard is the safer choice
inbounds.snellHint: Snell has one shared PSK: every user connects with the same key, so per-user restrictions and accounting do not apply. The share text is a Surge line.
inbounds.ingressSectionHint: Only for an IPLC / dedicated line in front of the node; most nodes never need it
inbounds.realityScanHint: Real TLS handshakes from the node: TLS 1.3, h2, X25519, certificate, and no public CDN.
inbounds.realityCdnHint: CDN-hosted sites get found by "preferred IP" scanners, whose users then relay traffic through your node
inbounds.fallbackLimitHint: Connections that fail REALITY auth are relayed to the target; throttled, a discovered node is worthless to scanners. Xray only.
inbounds.realityTargetHint: Current target: {{host}}. It must speak TLS 1.3 + h2 and not sit on Cloudflare or another CDN.
inbounds.realityNeedsNode: Save the node first to probe from it.
inbounds.tlsHint: REALITY needs no certificate; TLS needs one for the name
inbounds.ingressBindHint: Leave the listen address blank to bind the line IP {{ip}}.

ingress.title: Line ingresses
ingress.hint: Register an IPLC / dedicated line in front of the node: inbounds bind to the line NIC, entries advertise the provider's public entry, and lines without one are reached through a relay node forwarding to the far-end address. Any protocol may ride a line ingress; whether it passes depends on the provider's entry (nobrand's carrier entry, for one, only passes non-TLS protocols such as mieru). Direct access needs nothing here.
ingress.name: Name
ingress.bindIPHint: The line NIC address on this machine; inbounds bind to it (blank = all addresses)
ingress.lineIPHint: The line's address at the other end; relays forward here. Not reachable from the public internet
ingress.entryHostHint: Provider-supplied entry (e.g. a China Mobile entry IP) that clients dial; blank if none
ingress.entryDomainHint: A name for the public entry: share links use it instead of the IP. Point its DNS record at the public entry yourself.
ingress.portOffsetHint: entry port = local port + offset, usually 0
ingress.noEntryHint: This line has no public entry: add a port forward on a relay that can reach it (target = the far-end address) and share the relay's address.
ingress.deleteHint: Inbounds using it fall back to direct; share links change accordingly.
ingress.empty: No line ingresses. Only needed when an IPLC or dedicated line sits in front of this node.
ingress.reservedHint: Ports in the range the provider uses itself (usually the mapped SSH port), comma separated; recipes skip them and inbounds may not take them

routing.title: Outbounds & landing
routing.hint: Add exits (landing servers) to this node, then send all traffic or specific inbounds through one of them — a relay. An outbound can itself go via another outbound (chain). Changes apply within seconds.
routing.empty: No outbounds: everything leaves this machine directly.
routing.addFromLink: Add an outbound from a share link
routing.rawHint: Passed to the core untranslated in its own dialect; normally not needed.
routing.defaultHint: Traffic matching no rule goes here; picking an outbound relays the whole node.
routing.matchHint: Comma separated: inbound:tag, domain:example.com, full:host, ip:1.2.3.0/24, protocol:bittorrent, port:443

certs.title: Certificates
certs.subtitle: PEM pairs you upload are used ahead of automatic certificates for every inbound whose TLS name they cover (exact or wildcard).
certs.domainHint: Blank = the first name in the certificate; wildcards as *.example.com
certs.deleteHint: Inbounds covered by it fall back to automatic or local certificates.
certs.autoHint: Certificates bosun obtained itself for inbounds with “Automatic certificate”.

probe.title: Probe
probe.subtitle: Latency measured from this machine: carrier probe points, your own tasks and the RTT of each dedicated line from its NIC.
probe.resultsHint: Refreshed every 10 seconds. × means lost; lines are measured to their far-end address.
probe.noResults: No results yet. Turn the probe on below, or wait for the first samples.
probe.managedHint: Captain manages this node, so the panel's probe settings apply; these are read-only.
probe.enabledHint: Nothing runs while this is off.
probe.carrierHint: TCP-connect time to the CT/CU/CM probe points every 10 seconds; a refused connection still counts.
probe.carriersHint: One per line: name host:port. Blank = the default carrier points; anything here replaces the whole set.
probe.tasksHint: icmp / tcp / http checks or a download throughput test (a large file URL, run every 10 minutes at most). A source IP binds the probe to that NIC, e.g. to measure a dedicated line.

users.title: Users
users.subtitle: Who may use this node. Each user has a subscription link and traffic counters.
users.emptyHint: No users yet. Add one and send them the subscription link.
users.name: Name
users.quotaHint: 0 = unlimited; access stops when used up
users.onlineIps: Online IPs (visible on Xray and Hysteria cores)
users.subHint: Importing it gives the client every inbound this user may use.
users.rotateHint: The old link stops working immediately.

forwards.title: Forwards
forwards.subtitle: Relay TCP/UDP from a local port to the next hop, for relay chains.
forwards.backendRelayHint: bosun relays the bytes itself: domain targets, connection and byte counters.
forwards.backendNftHint: Kernel DNAT, fastest; needs the nft binary, an IPv4 literal target, and reports no byte counters.
forwards.targetNftHint: IPv4 address:port (nftables does not resolve names)
forwards.preserveSourceHint: No MASQUERADE: the target sees the real client address, so it must route replies back through this node or nothing connects.

settings.title: Settings
settings.subtitle: Node identity, login and mode.
settings.publicHostHint: Server address in share links; blank uses the address this panel was opened on.
settings.coresHint: bosun only runs tested upstream releases, downloaded on first use.
settings.certsHint: Inbounds with “Automatic certificate” use this account. HTTP needs port 80 reachable; DNS goes through Cloudflare.
settings.cfTokenHint: DNS challenge only; permission Zone.DNS edit
settings.panelDomainHint: Serves the panel over HTTPS with an automatic certificate; restart after saving

logs.title: Logs
logs.subtitle: Recent bosun log lines; use journalctl -u bosun for everything.

update.title: Version and updates
update.devBuild: Development build: online updates are not offered.
update.containerHint: A binary swapped inside the container is lost on the next recreate. Pull the new image on the host instead:
update.applyConfirm: Download {{version}}, verify it, replace the running binary and restart. Cores restart too, so users drop for a few seconds. Continue?
update.rollbackConfirm: Switch back to {{version}} and restart. Continue?
update.restartConfirm: The process exits and systemd or Docker starts it again; cores restart. Continue?
update.restartingHint: Waiting for the service to come back. The page reloads by itself and you stay signed in.
update.restartTimeout: No answer after 90 seconds. Startup may be slow or the upgrade failed; reload later and check the server logs if it persists.

komari.title: Komari reporting
komari.hint: Report this node to a Komari monitor as an agent: give the server URL and the auto-discovery key, the node registers itself, then sends CPU, memory, disk and network metrics every few seconds and answers Komari's ping tasks. No terminal, files or remote exec. Independent of the local probe.
komari.keyHint: Komari → Settings → General → auto-discovery key; used only for the first registration
komari.name: Display name
komari.nameHint: Blank = hostname; Komari prefixes it with Auto-

doctor.title: Doctor
doctor.subtitle: Read-only checks: cores, listeners, certificates, forwards, firewall, disk, panel link. Nothing is changed.

backup.title: Backup and restore
backup.hint: Download this node's whole configuration (inbounds, users, forwards, line ingresses, pushed certificates, Komari registration) as one archive; restoring replaces the current configuration with the archive's.
backup.restoreConfirm: The current inbounds, users, forwards and ingresses are replaced by the archive's and the cores restart. If the archive carries a different admin login you will be signed out. Continue?
backup.adminChanged: admin login changed, sign in again
backup.managedHint: Managed by Captain: the panel holds the configuration. Download only; restore is disabled.

outbound.title: Outbound
outbound.subtitle: Where this node's traffic goes: forward ports as-is to another machine (a front relay), or exit through a landing server (a relay).
